item.title: Through TOMORROW: Dan Charles Award nominations are open! Submit by June 30
item.description:
Dan Charles Award nominations open through TOMORROW! June 30 @ 5 p.m.

Tell us about an outstanding community member today!

 

 

Each year, the Dan Charles Award is presented a Columbus resident who is an active leader in their community, engages with diverse stakeholders and the City of Columbus, has a vision for their community, and makes change through service.

This year, we invite you to nominate a community leader who you think is deserving of the Dan Charles Award! You have until Tuesday, June 30, 2026 at 5 p.m. to submit nominations. 

 

The nomination should recognize a resident’s:

 

  • Role(s) as community leader
  • Engagement with diverse stakeholders and with the City of Columbus
  • Transformative vision for their community

 

Go to this link to nominate now: https://tinyurl.com/DanCharlesAward2026 

 

PAST RECIPIENTS

2011: Dan Charles, South Side CAN

2012: Lois Maier, Berwyn East, MAC, and Block Watch Coordinator

2013: Peggy Murphy, Greater Columbus Growing Coalition & Highland Avenue Garden

item.title: Let's talk local student success
item.description:
Join us to discuss local student success!
Tuesday, June 23, 2026, 6-7 p.m.

What have we accomplished? What else can we do?

Linden Branch, Columbus Metropolitan Library
2223 Cleveland Ave., Columbus, OH 43211

Join the Department of Neighborhoods for a cup of coffee as Director Kym Douglas guides a panel discussion on how local students are finding success in the classroom. We are going talk about Columbus' investment in that success and what new programs and efforts have been brought into the schools. A world cafe-style discussion with attendees will follow. 

 

Panelists will include a Columbus City Schools student and a parent, Hamilton STEM Principal Dr. Christopher Brady, Javier Negrete with The Ohio State University School of Social Work and Tifani Rey with Children's Hospital.

Register to attend now: 
https://tinyurl.com/4td9jfsa 

We hope to see you there!

item.title: TOMORROW! Ubuntu: Unity Conversations Across Cultures quarterly session
item.description:
Ubuntu: Unity Conversations Across Cultures quarterly session

TOMORROW!


Join us in-person for the next 2026 Ubuntu: Unity Conversations Across Cultures session on the theme "The Diaspora: Cultivating Growth and beauty in Columbus".

Tomorrow, Thursday, May 21, 2026 | 5-7:30 p.m.
Barnett Community Center
1184 Barnett Road, Columbus, OH 43227

Refreshments will be provided!

The City of Columbus' Ubuntu Series: Unity Conversations Across Cultures is a community discussion initiative operated by the City of Columbus Department of Neighborhoods. Rooted in the African philosophy of Ubuntu ("I am because we are"), the program aims to build bridges, heal community divisions, and promote civic engagement among diverse populations, particularly connecting New Americans, immigrants, refugees and long-term residents.

RSVP to our next session on May 21:

Ubuntu Conversation Series RSVP

If you have questions, please contact Lindora Howard-Diawara LKDiawara@columbus.gov.

item.title: Join us for One Columbus Culture Day on May 1!
item.description:
Join us for One Columbus Culture Day!

Friday, May 1, 2026, 4:30-7:30 p.m. at the North YMCA -- FREE

 

Dear community leaders, partners and friends,

 

The City of Columbus Department of Neighborhoods New American Program, in partnership with the North YMCA, will host the third annual “One Columbus Culture Day” on Friday, May 1, 2026, 4:30-7:30 p.m. at 1640 Sandalwood Place, Columbus, Ohio 43229.

 

This event is intended to help foster unity and collaboration. Please save-the-date and join us to celebrate our diverse cultures that make Columbus beautiful.

 

Bring your family and friends to get a lifetime experience of different international cuisines, performances, poetry and thematic stories -- all in one space.

 

If you have any questions, contact Lindora Howard-Diawara at LKDiawara@columbus.gov or 614-645-3284.

item.title: Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) planning meeting for West Broad Street
item.description:
Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) planning

Thursday, March 5th from 6 to 7 PM

 

 

Please join us for our first community meeting kicking off the Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) planning effort for the West Broad Street Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) corridor! The West Broad Street TOD Plan is intended to support the development of welcoming and accessible station areas that provide a wide variety of affordable and attainable housing, support existing businesses, attract new investment and job creation, and enhance, preserve and protect each neighborhood’s rich, diverse community heritage and local character.

 

The community-wide kickoff meeting will be held Thursday, March 5th from 6 to 7 PM at the Columbus Metropolitan Library Hilltop Branch at 511 S. Hague Avenue in meeting rooms 2, 3, and 4. Click here to RSVP, and learn more about this exciting effort! We encourage you to share the attached flyer and the website link with your networks.

item.title: FREE Black History Month film screening: Genius: MLK/X
item.description:
FREE Black History Month film screening "Genius: MLK/X"

Saturday, Feb. 28, 2026 | 2–5 PM
COSI Giant Screen Theater | 333 W. Broad St.


Join the City of Columbus Department of Neighborhoods as we close out the “One Dream, Many Voices” event series with a special Black History Month community screening of Genius: MLK/X (Rated TV-14), in COSI’s Giant Screen Theater.

 

This limited series explores the formative years and intersecting paths of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and Malcolm X. Episodes 1 and 2 will be shown, featuring pivotal moments such as Malcolm’s release from prison, MLK’s university graduation, and the foundations of their ideological differences - all set against the backdrop of a changing America.

 

FREE snacks and popcorn will be provided. Pre-registration is required. Link to RSVP: https://blackhistoryscreening.eventbrite.com

item.description:
Ubuntu session 1 of 2026 is here!

 

Dear Community leaders, Partners and Friends,

 

The Department of Neighborhoods will host its first 2026 session of the “Ubuntu Series: Unity Conversations Across Cultures” this week. The theme this time around is “Columbus’ Black Diaspora: United we stand, divided we fall.”

item.title: Join us for the MLK Day March and Program!
item.description:
Join us for the MLK Day March and Program!


Just a few days away! Join us for the City of Columbus' annual MLK Day March and Program.

Hosted by the Department of Neighborhoods, the City of Columbus’ annual Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. March will start from the Historic St. Paul African Methodist Episcopal (AME) Church and the Program will be held at the Historic Lincoln Theatre. After the pre-march event and neighborhood march, the theatre event will take place.

If the march is cancelled due to inclement weather, media will be notified, and the theatre program will take place during its originally scheduled time of 4:30 p.m.

The event is free and open to the public. If one wishes to be part of the march, simply show up at St. Paul AME Church beginning at 3 p.m.

ADA assistance will be provided as part of the march by COTA Mainstream. Those in need may board the COTA ADA transit vehicle, which will travel with the march.

 

WHEN:     
Monday, Jan. 19, 2026
3-5:30 p.m. (includes both march and program)

 

WHERE:   

March: St. Paul AME Church 639 E. Long St. Columbus, Ohio 3 p.m.

 

Program: Historic Lincoln Theatre
769 E. Long St. Columbus, OH 43203 4:30 p.m.

Parking is available across the street from the church as well as across the street from the theatre and on the street.

item.title: Registration Now Open! 25th Annual MLK Youth Oratorical Contest
item.description:
Calling All Student Voices: Register Today for the 25th Annual MLK Oratorical Contest!

 

We’re excited to announce that registration is now open for the 25th Annual Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Youth Oratorical Contest -  happening Saturday, Feb. 7, 2026 at Columbus State Community College!

This is a powerful opportunity for students in grades K–12 to speak truth, build confidence, and honor the legacy of Dr. King.

This year marks the 25th anniversary of the contest, and we want you to be part of the celebration!

✅ Students in grades K–12 are eligible
✅ Winners advance to represent Columbus in the state competition
✅ Free to participate – snacks and lunch provided!

We’re also calling on:

  • Educators who see promise in their students
  • Mentors who help young people find their voice
  • Parents, grandparents, caregivers who know their child has something meaningful to say
  • Community leaders and advocates who want to see youth rise

Encourage a young person to sign up. Be the reason they stand in front of a microphone and speak their truth.

Event Date: Saturday, Feb. 7, 2026
Location: Columbus State Community College (Center for Workforce Development)
315 Cleveland Ave., Columbus, OH 43215
Time: 9:00 AM – 2:00 PM

🔗 REGISTER NOW: 2026 MLK Oratorical Contest

Submission Deadline: Monday, Jan. 26, 2026 at 5:00 PM

Have questions? Contact Grace Hunter at grace@paraclete-planning.com or 614-266-8150.

item.title: Save the date!
item.description:
Celebrating 25 years of student voice and leadership!

Dear Educators, Coaches, and Community Leaders,

We’re excited to announce that the 25th Annual Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Youth Oratorical Contest will take place on Saturday, Feb. 7, 2026, from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Columbus State Community College!

This year marks a major milestone — the 25th anniversary of this transformative contest! We’ll be celebrating not only the incredible young voices of today, but also the legacy of students who have taken the stage over the past two decades. This year's contest theme is:

“I Am a New Generation Leader: An Architect of Transformational Change.”

Students in grades K–12 across the City of Columbus are eligible to participate, and we’re counting on YOU to help us identify, inspire and coach the next generation of leaders!

Applications will open soon! Stay tuned for details and the official registration link.

Please share this date with your colleagues, school administrators and youth-serving teams so we can continue the tradition of excellence that has defined this contest for 25 years.

For questions or more information, visit columbus.gov/neighborhoods or call 614-645-1993.

Thank you for your continued partnership in empowering our city's youth. We can't wait to see what this year’s voices will bring!
